translations.text: For years now I have been considering how to keep anyone from finding anything to say against me in any way.
For I know that there can be no justice among people without a true standard, especially among a multitude with no one to guide them in equality.
They will be like a ship full of holes, whose sailing you cannot trust from one shore of the sea to the other, not to mention its open waters.
Some tell lies about bodily needs; others grumble about these same provisions. Some want to steal, or indeed are stealing; others find fault.
Some act with lies, others with an alien heart; some want to give orders on their own, while others want to find comfort for themselves,
whether they are sick or well. For this happens among many people: they say that they live in fellowship with one another, but they do not do so sincerely.
No one who truly lives in community will ever seek comfort for themselves alone and abandon any of those who share communal life with them.
Perfect communal life means living in this same equality. And woe to those who live in these places at any time if they follow other ways that show favoritism.
For this reason, I order that these three kinds of food always be kept in these places for those among you who are sick: fish [?], cheese prepared as they want
it, whether dry or salted, and eggs, whether salted or, if they want to boil them, boiled fresh, or prepared however they want.
Only, no one among you, whether male or female, is ever to eat such things except those who are genuinely sick and have been recognized as such.
by all the faithful brothers, and especially by the fathers of these places at any given time, who will give an account to God for those gathered in them.
No one is to eat such things anywhere except in the place set aside for the sick alone,
where they ask for a little wine.

They will also look for these other things, and they will also be kept in the storeroom, so that whoever is in charge, or will be in charge, of these places may always give them what they need, after considering the condition

of the person and his illness, with thirteen people among you always serving as witnesses for those who have come to need such things. They are to give these things to them in the proper measure, in fear
of the one into whose hands we shall all come, at the time when no one, whether male or female in these congregations, will be able to think of sleep.
